0.content: Emilie named and invented her own profession. When the Maison Gardiennage closes a case, she shows her signed power-of-attorney papers and confidentiality agreement, steps over the cordon and restores the scene. Bodies and badly damaged objects have already been removed. She removes bloodstains, tissue and fragments with chemicals she adapted from test reagents. She asks nothing beyond the cleanup parameters, but from spatter, residue and how objects fell she can often piece together what happened. Afterwards she changes back into her own clothes in silence and nods to the clean room, feeling that part of the dead has only now been laid to rest.

1.content: Emilie is the most famous perfume designer in Fontaine, works for no brand (not even the Confrerie of Cabriere), and calls perfumery her hobby. For her, perfume is close to a chemistry experiment and the perfumer bridges art and science. Once a perfume is sold, its meaning belongs to the wearer: Marcotte may smell like childhood to her and like love or regret to someone else. Her products sell out, with queues before dawn, while practical designs like insect-repellent perfume or a scent for Melusines never reach shop shelves.

2.content: Emilie's 4.8 Story Quest. Nearly twenty years ago Fontaine's Perfume Mania drove "Auguste" to ten million Mora a bottle; its flower then vanished in a fire. Rumours of the flower reappearing in Sumeru and a wave of counterfeits compared to her work brought Emilie to a flower exhibition at Port Ormos. She hoped to puncture the myth. There she met the Traveler, cured Paimon's pollen sneezing, and reunited with her old teacher "Edgar", one of Auguste's creators, along with the merchant brothers Sylvain and Lucien, newly out of the Fortress of Meropide. "Edgar" was apparently attacked, Lucien died, and the truth emerged: the flower was grown by Yelena, an exiled Fatuus, with a Delusion that ruined her body, and she burned her garden and herself to hide the evidence.

3.content: When Emilie's parents moved to Sumeru for work, the child Emilie studied perfumery basics under "Edgar", a Fontainian perfumer who had served a short sentence as an accomplice in the Auguste fraud and now only taught. He taught her that an accord can recreate scents that cannot be extracted, though "certain fragrances are simply one of a kind." Years later she learned he was Kirya, the young brother of the Fatuus Yelena, seeking revenge for her death. She stopped him and saved his life, and still called him "Master" to the end.

4.content: Emilie and Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, met through work, but their conversations are rarely serious. Chevreuse relies on Emilie's chemistry to identify a suspect's perfume, a bouquet's flowers or the soil on their boots, and says she has never been wrong. Chevreuse once called her unromantic. Emilie answered that perfumers who chase romance make bad perfume. Chevreuse loves crime novels mostly to argue about legal liability, and Emilie collects real news. Neither is the romantic one, and they think alike.

5.content: Chiori, the designer, has a keen eye for trends and always picks the one of Emilie's test perfumes that will sell best. Under their business arrangement Emilie supplies small quantities of new perfumes to Chioriya Boutique; Eloffe sprays them in the fitting room, and Chiori passes on customer feedback. No customer has ever complained, and many ask where to buy the scent. Chiori buys a bottle herself whenever a release reaches the shops. Visiting Emilie's spotless home, she asked bluntly whether it was some kind of compulsion; Emilie laughed: "It has to be this way, that's all."
